report_meta.supply_chain_link: Marvell is a connective HUB in this graph and plays THREE roles at once. (1) It is a COMPONENT supplier INSIDE other companies' optical transceivers — its optical DSPs, TIAs, and drivers go into modules made by Applied Optoelectronics (reports/Applied Optoelectronics.json), Coherent (reports/Coherent.json), Lumentum (reports/Lumentum.json), and InnoLight. (2) It is a custom-AI-silicon (XPU/ASIC) maker for hyperscalers (AWS, Microsoft, Google, Meta) — these custom accelerators are the merchant-GPU ALTERNATIVE that competes directly with NVIDIA (reports/NVIDIA.json), alongside Broadcom. (3) It is now also an NVIDIA PARTNER: an expanded deal integrates Marvell custom silicon + optics into NVIDIA's ecosystem via NVLink Fusion, plus AI RAN — and NVIDIA took an equity stake. KEY INSIGHT: NVIDIA has now invested in / partnered with Coherent, Lumentum AND Marvell — wiring the optical + custom-silicon ecosystem around itself. So Marvell both competes with NVIDIA (custom XPUs) and feeds it (optics, NVLink bridge) — classic 'co-opetition.' Upstream, Marvell relies on TSMC for manufacturing and on InP lasers (from Lumentum/Coherent) for its optical modules; it also bought Polariton (plasmonic photonics) and Celestial AI (photonic fabric) to extend its optics roadmap.

beginner_glossary.Fabless semiconductor company: A chip company that DESIGNS chips but doesn't own factories — it outsources manufacturing (Marvell relies on TSMC). This keeps capital costs lower but makes it dependent on its foundry partner.
beginner_glossary.Data infrastructure semiconductors: Chips that move, store, process, and secure data at large scale — Marvell's focus. As of FY2026, data center is >75% of revenue.
beginner_glossary.Custom silicon / ASIC / XPU: A chip designed for ONE customer's specific need. Hyperscalers (AWS, Google, Microsoft, Meta) hire Marvell to co-design custom AI accelerators ('XPUs') instead of only buying NVIDIA's off-the-shelf GPUs. This is Marvell's marquee growth business (target >$10B by fiscal 2029).
beginner_glossary.Merchant silicon: The opposite of custom — a standard chip sold to everyone (e.g., an NVIDIA GPU). Marvell's NVLink Fusion deal lets hyperscalers 'mix and match' custom (Marvell) and merchant (NVIDIA) chips.
beginner_glossary.XPU-attach: The supporting chips that sit NEXT TO an accelerator — network interface cards (NICs), CXL memory controllers, retimers, etc. Marvell has 10+ XPU-attach programs; a fast-growing add-on to its custom business.
beginner_glossary.DSP (digital signal processor) / optical: The chip inside an optical transceiver that cleans up and encodes the high-speed signal. 'PAM4' is the encoding method. Marvell is the long-time leader in optical PAM4 DSPs — these go inside transceivers made by AAOI, Coherent, Lumentum, etc.
beginner_glossary.TIA / driver: Transimpedance amplifier (TIA) and laser driver — analog chips that pair with the DSP and laser inside a transceiver. Marvell's TIA+driver business is scaling toward a $1B+ annual run rate.
beginner_glossary.SerDes: Serializer/Deserializer — the high-speed circuit that sends data in and out of a chip. Marvell's best-in-class SerDes is a core enabler of its switches, custom chips, and interconnect (a key competitive edge).
beginner_glossary.Interconnect: The broad category of chips/modules that connect things in a data center (optical DSPs, DCI modules, TIAs, drivers, retimers, AECs). Marvell's LARGEST data-center business, growing >70% YoY in FY2027.
beginner_glossary.DCI (data center interconnect) / ZR / ZR: Pluggable optical modules that link data centers to each other over distance. ZR/ZR+ are the long-reach 'coherent' types. Marvell pioneered pluggable DCI and ships to all 5 major US hyperscalers.
beginner_glossary.Coherent DSP / CoherentLight: 'Coherent' optics carry data farther (kilometers). Marvell's 'CoherentLight' is a low-power coherent product for 2–20 km links inside/between data-center campuses. (Note: 'coherent' the technology is unrelated to the company Coherent Corp.)
beginner_glossary.Scale-out / scale-up / scale-across: Three layers of AI networking. Scale-out = connecting many systems in a building. Scale-up = connecting chips inside one system (the newest, biggest opportunity). Scale-across = connecting different data centers (huge bandwidth, where DCI booms). Marvell sells into all three.
beginner_glossary.Switching (Ethernet switch, 51.2T, 100T): The chip that routes data between many connections. Capacity is measured in terabits (e.g., 51.2T, new 100T, roadmap to 200T). Marvell's scale-out switch business is heading past $1B annual revenue.
beginner_glossary.UALink / eSUN / NVLink: Competing standards for 'scale-up' switching (connecting accelerators tightly). UALink and eSUN (Ethernet-based) are open standards; NVLink is NVIDIA's. Marvell builds for all three (and bridges to NVLink via the NVIDIA partnership).
beginner_glossary.PCIe / CXL switch: Standards for connecting CPUs, accelerators, and memory. CXL lets systems add/share memory pools — increasingly important for AI inference. Marvell added these via its XConn acquisition.
beginner_glossary.NVLink Fusion: An NVIDIA program that lets third-party custom chips (like Marvell's) plug into NVIDIA's NVLink ecosystem. The core of Marvell's expanded NVIDIA partnership — Marvell becomes the 'bridge' between custom and NVIDIA architectures.
beginner_glossary.Silicon photonics / NPO / CPO / light en: Building optical functions on silicon. NPO (near-package optics) and CPO (co-packaged optics) put the optics next to the chip to save power for 'scale-up.' A 'light engine' is Marvell's silicon-photonics optical building block (now 3rd-gen, 6.4T).
beginner_glossary.Modulator types (MZM / EAM / MRM) & plas: Different ways to imprint data onto light. Marvell supports all the mainstream types (MZM, EAM, MRM). Its Polariton acquisition adds 'plasmonics' — modulators with >1 THz bandwidth (~10x today's silicon photonics) for future ultra-high speeds.
beginner_glossary.Photonic fabric (Celestial AI): An optical interconnect 'fabric' that links accelerators and memory with light; Marvell bought Celestial AI for this, and a tier-1 hyperscaler already selected it for next-gen XPU scale-up.
beginner_glossary.AEC (active electrical cable) / retimer: An AEC is a smart copper cable with chips inside for short, cheap, reliable links; a retimer cleans up high-speed signals over distance. Marvell's 'golden cable' AEC and retimers compete with Credo and Astera Labs.
beginner_glossary.AI RAN / OCTEON: OCTEON is Marvell's processor for telecom base stations. 'AI RAN' = running 5G/6G radio AND AI workloads on the same hardware. The NVIDIA partnership pairs OCTEON with NVIDIA GPUs for this.
beginner_glossary.Hyperscaler / cloud capex: Hyperscalers are the giant clouds (AWS, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle). 'Cloud capex' is how much they spend building data centers — the key driver of Marvell's demand. Marvell assumes it grows 30%+ in fiscal 2028.
beginner_glossary.GAAP vs non-GAAP: GAAP = official accounting (includes acquisition amortization, stock-based comp, one-time tax items). Non-GAAP = adjusted. For Marvell the two differ a LOT and can flip direction: a one-time tax benefit pushed FY2026 GAAP ABOVE non-GAAP, while acquisition accounting pushed Q1 FY2027 GAAP far BELOW non-GAAP. Read both.
beginner_glossary.Prepayments: Cash Marvell pays suppliers in advance to lock up scarce manufacturing capacity. It plans ~$1B of prepayments in fiscal 2027 to secure supply for its growth.
beginner_glossary.P/E and P/S: P/E = price ÷ earnings per share; P/S = market value ÷ revenue. Marvell's GAAP P/E (~97x) is high; analysts focus on non-GAAP and on the fast-falling forward P/S as revenue ramps.

company_snapshot.what_it_is: Marvell is a fabless 'data infrastructure' semiconductor company. It designs the connectivity and custom-compute chips that move, switch, and process data inside AI data centers — optical DSPs and interconnect, Ethernet switches, data-center-interconnect (DCI) modules, and custom AI accelerators (XPUs) for hyperscalers. Over the past decade it transformed from a consumer-chip maker into an AI-infrastructure pure-play, with data center now >75% of revenue.
company_snapshot.ceo: Matthew J. Murphy (Chair & CEO); Willem A. Meintjes (CFO); Christopher Koopmans (operations/COO); Sandeep Bharathi (engineering)
company_snapshot.founded: 1995. Re-built through ~$36B of M&A over the past decade (Cavium, Inphi, Innovium, Avera) plus FY2027 deals (Celestial AI, XConn, Polariton), alongside heavy organic R&D.
company_snapshot.where_it_sits_in_the_chain: Component tier (optical DSPs, TIAs, drivers, SerDes, retimers) AND switch_system tier (Ethernet switches, DCI modules, custom XPUs). Both a competitor to NVIDIA (custom silicon) and a supplier into the optical chain (DSPs inside AAOI/Coherent/Lumentum transceivers) and an NVIDIA partner (NVLink Fusion).
company_snapshot.manufacturing_note: Fabless — manufacturing outsourced primarily to TSMC (2nm/advanced nodes). To handle the AI surge, Marvell is making ~$1B of supplier prepayments in fiscal 2027 to lock up capacity, following the same playbook it used in the last supply crunch.
products: Interconnect (largest DC business): optical PAM4 DSPs (800G, 1.6T/200G-per-lane), TIAs & drivers, CoherentLight, pluggable DCI (ZR/ZR+), retimers, AECs
Custom silicon: flagship XPU (AI accelerator) + 10+ XPU-attach programs (NIC, CXL memory) for hyperscalers
Switching: scale-out Ethernet (12.8T / 51.2T / new 100T, roadmap to 200T); emerging scale-up switching (UALink, eSUN, NVLink)
Scale-up optics: silicon-photonics light engines (NPO/CPO), Celestial AI photonic fabric, Polariton plasmonics
PCIe / CXL switches & memory expanders (via XConn)
Communications & other: enterprise networking, carrier (OCTEON / AI RAN), consumer — smaller, slower-growing

business_model.summary: Marvell makes money selling AI-data-center connectivity and custom-compute chips. The thesis: as AI models get bigger, the bottleneck shifts from raw compute to CONNECTIVITY (moving data between chips, systems, and data centers) — and Marvell has the industry's broadest interconnect portfolio plus a fast-growing custom-silicon franchise. It wins multi-year, multi-generation designs with hyperscalers, then layers on attach products. Growth is gated mainly by supply, so Marvell prepays suppliers to lock capacity.
how_they_make_money: Data center (76% of Q1 FY2027 revenue, $1.8B): three sub-businesses — Interconnect (largest), Switching, and Custom silicon. Grew 46% YoY in FY2026 and guided ~50% in FY2027, ~55% in FY2028.
Interconnect: optical DSPs, TIAs/drivers, DCI modules, CoherentLight, retimers, AECs — growing >70% YoY in FY2027; the single biggest driver.
Custom silicon: co-designing XPUs and attach chips for hyperscalers — >20% growth in FY2027, more than doubling in FY2028, targeting >$10B by FY2029.
Switching: scale-out Ethernet (>$600M in FY2027, doubling) plus an emerging scale-up switch business (UALink/eSUN/NVLink).
Communications & other ($585M in Q1 FY2027): enterprise, carrier (OCTEON), consumer — recovered from an inventory correction; ~10% growth in FY2027, low-single-digit in FY2028.
competitive_moat_analyst_view: Broadest interconnect portfolio + first-to-market PAM4 cadence: Marvell leads successive optical-DSP generations (800G → 1.6T → 400G-per-lane), the backbone of AI networking. [Q1 FY2027 call]

Best-in-class SerDes + high-speed IO + advanced packaging: the hard-to-replicate building blocks that win custom XPU and switch sockets ('really it is us and maybe a couple of other people that can do this'). [Q1 FY2027 call]
End-to-end breadth: Marvell can offer XPU + switch + optics together — a full AI-infrastructure solution few rivals match; strengthened by Celestial AI + XConn + Polariton. [Q1 FY2027 call]
Deep hyperscaler relationships: custom engagements across all 5 US hyperscalers; ships DCI to all five; multi-year locked programs. [Q1 FY2027 call]
NVIDIA partnership (NVLink Fusion + optics + AI RAN) positions Marvell as the neutral 'bridge' between custom and NVIDIA architectures. [Q1 FY2027 call]
facts: Q1 FY2027 (reported 2026-05-27): record revenue $2.418B, +28% YoY, +9% QoQ; data center 76% of revenue. [Q1 FY2027 call]
Raised FY2027 revenue outlook to ~$11.5B (+~40% YoY) and FY2028 to ~$16.5B (+~45% YoY). [Q1 FY2027 call]

Planning ~$1B of supplier prepayments in FY2027 to secure capacity. [Q1 FY2027 call]

revenue_streams.analyst_view: Marvell is now an AI-data-center company (76% of revenue, growing ~50%) with a legacy comms tail (~24%, low growth). Within data center, the three engines have different profiles: Interconnect is the biggest and fastest right now (>70% YoY), riding the copper-to-optical shift and the rise of scale-across DCI; Custom silicon is the highest-visibility multi-year story (target >$10B by FY2029); Switching is an emerging share-gainer. Because demand exceeds supply, near-term revenue is gated by capacity (hence the $1B prepayments), not orders.

industry_trends.trend: Connectivity is the new AI bottleneck
industry_trends.why_it_matters: As models scale (reasoning, mixture-of-experts, agents), moving data between chips/systems/data centers matters as much as compute — directly expanding Marvell's interconnect and switching TAM.
industry_trends.evidence: Management: 'AI infrastructure performance is increasingly defined by connectivity, not just compute or memory'; interconnect raised to >70% YoY. [Computex 2026, 2026-06-01; Q1 FY2027 call]

industry_trends.why_it_matters: As speeds rise, links move from copper to optics deeper inside the data center — growing demand for Marvell's optical DSPs, silicon photonics, and light engines.
industry_trends.evidence: 'Systems transition from copper to optical… already underway and will accelerate over the next year'; scale-up optics (NPO/CPO) forecast to ~$300M next year. [Computex 2026; Q1 FY2027 call]

industry_trends.why_it_matters: Hyperscalers want their own accelerators (cheaper, tuned to their workloads). Marvell (with Broadcom) is the key enabler — the merchant-GPU alternative to NVIDIA.
industry_trends.evidence: Custom revenue >20% FY2027, more than doubling FY2028, target >$10B FY2029 (implied ~20% of a ~$55B custom TAM). [Q1 FY2027 call]

industry_trends.why_it_matters: Power/space limits force AI clusters to span multiple buildings; the back-end network must extend between them, with bandwidth ~10x today's front-end DCI.
industry_trends.evidence: Pluggable DCI TAM expanding; Marvell's secure 1.6T ZR/ZR+ (2nm coherent DSP) sampling this year; DCI to ~$1B annualized in FY2028 (double FY2026's ~$500M). [Q1 FY2027 call]

industry_trends.trend: Scale-up networking is the next big greenfield
industry_trends.why_it_matters: Tightly connecting many accelerators needs high-radix switches and high-bandwidth optics — a large new market with no established leader.
industry_trends.evidence: Scale-up switching via UALink/eSUN/NVLink; each tier-1 engagement a 'multibillion-dollar lifetime' opportunity; scale-up optics ramping (Celestial AI fabric selected by a tier-1 hyperscaler). [Q1 FY2027 call]

industry_trends.trend: Agentic AI multiplies traffic and memory needs
industry_trends.why_it_matters: Agents query models many times per request and route across the cluster — increasing data movement, switching, CPUs, NICs, and memory (CXL) attach.
industry_trends.evidence: Cited as a tailwind for interconnect, switching, and XPU-attach; CXL memory adoption rising with inference/KV-caching. [Q1 FY2027 call]

industry_trends.trend: Supply-constrained AI semis → prepayments & vendor lock-in
industry_trends.why_it_matters: Everything touching AI has been capacity-constrained since 2020; suppliers reward partners who commit long-term demand and cash.
industry_trends.evidence: ~$1B of FY2027 prepayments; 5-year forecasts shared with a small set of key suppliers. [Q1 FY2027 call]

competitors.landscape_summary: Marvell competes across several markets, and its #1 rival in almost all of them is Broadcom — in custom ASICs, Ethernet switching, and optical/DSP. In custom AI silicon it also competes with smaller ASIC-design houses (Alchip, GUC) and, indirectly, with NVIDIA's merchant GPUs. In connectivity adjacencies it faces Credo (AECs) and Astera Labs (retimers/PCIe-CXL). Uniquely, NVIDIA is both a competitor (custom XPUs displace GPUs) and a partner/investor (NVLink Fusion) — 'co-opetition.'

key_competitors.note: The principal rival across custom ASICs (Google TPU, Meta MTIA), Ethernet switching (Tomahawk/Jericho), and optical. Larger and highly profitable — the benchmark to beat.
Competitor AND partner: Marvell's custom XPUs are the alternative to NVIDIA GPUs, but NVLink Fusion + the optics/AI-RAN deal make NVIDIA a collaborator and investor (see reports/NVIDIA.json).
Leader in active electrical cables (AECs); competes with Marvell's 'golden cable' program.
Connectivity specialist (retimers, PCIe/CXL) — competes with Marvell's retimer and XConn-based PCIe/CXL products.
Taiwanese custom-ASIC design houses competing for hyperscaler XPU sockets.
Optical transceiver/laser makers — Marvell SUPPLIES DSPs/TIAs into them, but also competes as it moves up into optics (silicon photonics, light engines).
Networking incumbent (switching/optics) — competes in parts of the data-center networking stack.

market_share_facts: Marvell is the long-time leader in merchant optical PAM4 DSPs and a top-2 custom-ASIC house (with Broadcom); it ships DCI to all 5 major US hyperscalers. [Q1 FY2027 call, 2026-05-27]
Custom-silicon target of >$10B by fiscal 2029 implies ~20% of a ~$55B custom TAM (management's framework). [Q1 FY2027 call]
competitors.supply_chain_cross_reference: Marvell's rival/partner NVIDIA, optical partners-and-rivals Coherent/Lumentum/AAOI, and foundry TSMC are all nodes in this repo. NVIDIA's investments in Coherent + Lumentum and its NVLink-Fusion partnership with Marvell show NVIDIA wiring the optical + custom-silicon ecosystem around itself.
competitors.differentiation_analyst_view: Marvell's edge is breadth + best-in-class SerDes/IO + an end-to-end story (XPU + switch + optics under one roof). Its central competitive risk is Broadcom (larger, higher-margin, and the custom-ASIC leader). A second nuance: in optics Marvell both supplies and competes with Coherent/Lumentum, and in custom it competes with the very GPU vendor (NVIDIA) it now partners with — a balance it must manage.

financial_performance.analyst_view: Financially this is a rapid, multi-year ramp with real operating leverage: revenue guided ~+40% (FY2027) then ~+45% (FY2028), with non-GAAP operating margin heading toward 38–40%. Two things a careful reader must hold: (1) GAAP earnings are noisy and can sit far below OR above non-GAAP depending on acquisition accounting and tax items — so judge the core business on non-GAAP and on cash flow (record $639M in Q1); and (2) the story leans heavily on guidance and on a few large custom programs and new markets (scale-up) executing — strong, but more forward-looking than a steady-state business.

That embeds years of ~40–45% revenue growth, the custom ramp toward >$10B (FY2029), and success in new scale-up markets. If those deliver, the multiple looks more reasonable on FY2028–2029 numbers; if cloud capex slows, Broadcom takes share, or a key custom program slips, the wide 52-week range ($61→$324) shows the downside.

valuation.analyst_view: Valuation is demanding but, unlike the optical pure-plays, supported by a clear multi-year revenue framework (FY2027 ~$11.5B → FY2028 ~$16.5B → custom >$10B by FY2029). The notable signal is that the stock trades ABOVE the analyst consensus (~$233) — the market is pricing in upside beyond Street models, leaving little room for execution stumbles. GAAP P/E is not the right lens here; the debate is durability of cloud capex, share vs Broadcom, and the custom/scale-up ramp.

growth_drivers.detail: Largest DC business; 800G strong, 1.6T/200G-per-lane ramping, 400G-per-lane next; TIAs/drivers toward $1B+ run-rate.
growth_drivers.evidence: Interconnect raised to >70% YoY FY2027. [Q1 FY2027 call, 2026-05-27]

growth_drivers.detail: Flagship XPU + new tier-1 XPU + 10+ attach programs (NIC, CXL); >20% FY2027, >2x FY2028, >$10B FY2029 target.
AI clusters spanning data centers; 1.6T ZR/ZR+ with 2nm coherent DSP; DCI to ~$1B annualized FY2028 (2x FY2026).
Silicon-photonics light engines (6.4T), Celestial AI photonic fabric (tier-1 win), Polariton plasmonics; ~$300M next year (>2x prior outlook).
Scale-out >$600M FY2027 (2x), >$1B FY2028; scale-up via UALink/eSUN/NVLink (XConn), each engagement multi-billion lifetime.
NVLink Fusion (custom-to-NVIDIA bridge), optics/silicon-photonics collaboration, AI RAN (OCTEON + NVIDIA GPUs); NVIDIA equity stake.
'Golden cable' AEC wins at 3 tier-1 hyperscalers; retimers ramping; PCIe Gen6/CXL 3.1 via XConn; combined AEC+retimer >2x FY2027.
Non-GAAP opex grows mid-to-high-teens% vs ~45% revenue growth → operating margin toward 38–40% in FY2028.
Polariton plasmonic modulators (>1 THz, ~10x silicon photonics) extend the roadmap to 3.2T+.
Ongoing buybacks (to manage dilution) plus a token dividend; record operating cash flow funds growth + returns.

risks.why_it_matters: Demand depends on a handful of hyperscalers' AI spending; Marvell itself assumes capex growth moderates to ~30%+ in FY2028. A bigger slowdown would hit hard.
Broadcom is larger and the leader in custom ASICs, switching, and optics. Losing key custom sockets or DSP share to Broadcom is the central competitive threat.
The custom ramp leans on a few large XPU programs (incl. a new tier-1 program); any cancellation, delay, or in-sourcing by a hyperscaler would dent the multi-year target.
~28x trailing / ~21x forward sales and a price ABOVE the ~$233 analyst consensus leave little room for stumbles; the 52-week range ($61→$324) shows the volatility.
1.6T, scale-up optics, scale-up switching, new XPU, DCI, AECs — all ramping at once and integrating three acquisitions (Celestial AI, XConn, Polariton). Complexity raises slip risk.
Growth is gated by supply; Marvell is prepaying ~$1B to secure it, but capacity or TSMC node constraints could cap revenue.
Acquisition amortization, earn-outs, and tax items make GAAP earnings swing widely (GAAP > non-GAAP in FY2026, but ≪ non-GAAP in Q1 FY2027), complicating analysis and optics.
Marvell both supplies (DSPs) and competes (silicon photonics) with Coherent/Lumentum/AAOI, and competes-yet-partners with NVIDIA — relationships that could shift.
Shares issued for acquisitions and the NVIDIA investment raised the count (~875M basic → ~915M diluted); buybacks only partly offset.
CXL-attach demand and comms recovery are tied to memory pricing and broader IT spending cycles.

scenarios.disclaimer: Illustrative scenarios to frame the range of outcomes — NOT predictions, targets, or advice.

bull_case.thesis: AI capex stays strong, custom silicon inflects toward >$10B (FY2029), interconnect keeps outgrowing capex, and scale-up (optics + switching) becomes a major new franchise — all with expanding margins.
key_drivers: Interconnect compounds (1.6T, DCI to $1B+, AECs/retimers); 400G-per-lane keeps the first-to-market lead.
Custom more than doubles in FY2028; the new tier-1 XPU ramps and additional sockets convert.
Scale-up optics and switching (Celestial AI, XConn, UALink/eSUN/NVLink) become real revenue.
NVIDIA partnership (NVLink Fusion) opens new mix-and-match opportunities.
Operating margin reaches the 38–40% target; the forward multiple compresses on rising EPS.
bull_case.what_to_watch: Custom program ramps; interconnect growth rate; scale-up optics/switch revenue starting; margin path to 38–40%.

base_case.thesis: Strong, supply-gated growth roughly in line with guidance (~40% FY2027, ~45% FY2028), with Broadcom remaining a tough competitor and scale-up still early.
key_drivers: Data center grows ~50%/~55%; interconnect leads; custom doubles in FY2028 as guided.
Margins expand toward the high-30s% with operating leverage.
Marvell holds DSP leadership and wins its share of custom sockets (alongside Broadcom).
Scale-up optics/switching contribute modestly, with the bigger payoff in FY2028+.
Stock tracks earnings growth; multiple stays premium but de-rates gradually.
base_case.what_to_watch: Quarterly revenue/margin trend vs guide; cloud-capex commentary; custom and DCI cadence; share count.

bear_case.thesis: Cloud capex slows or a key custom program slips, Broadcom takes share, and a stock priced above consensus de-rates sharply.
key_drivers: Hyperscaler capex decelerates faster than the assumed ~30%+; orders soften.
A flagship/new XPU program is delayed, resized, or in-sourced; custom target slips.
Broadcom wins key switching/custom/optics sockets; DSP pricing pressure rises.
Scale-up ramps disappoint or arrive late; integration of Celestial/XConn/Polariton drags.
Multiple compresses from ~28x sales (recall the $61 low).
bear_case.what_to_watch: Any capex guidance cut; custom program news; Broadcom design wins; gross-margin reversal; GAAP/non-GAAP gaps.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: Marvell Technology (MRVL) is a fabless 'data infrastructure' chip company that has reinvented itself, via ~$36B of M&A plus heavy R&D, into an AI-data-center pure-play (data center is 76% of revenue). It makes the CONNECTIVITY and CUSTOM-COMPUTE chips that AI clusters depend on — optical DSPs and interconnect (its biggest, fastest business, >70% YoY), Ethernet switches, data-center-interconnect modules, and custom AI accelerators (XPUs) for hyperscalers — which makes it simultaneously a key NVIDIA competitor (custom silicon is the alternative to GPUs, alongside Broadcom), a supplier into the optical chain (its DSPs go inside AAOI/Coherent/Lumentum transceivers), and an NVIDIA partner (NVLink Fusion, optics, AI RAN, plus an NVIDIA equity stake). The financials are inflecting hard: FY2026 revenue was a record $8.195B (+42%); Q1 FY2027 (reported 2026-05-27) hit a record $2.418B (+28% YoY) at 58.9% non-GAAP gross margin and 35% non-GAAP operating margin, with $718M non-GAAP net income and record $639M operating cash flow. Management RAISED its outlook to ~$11.5B for FY2027 (+~40%) and ~$16.5B for FY2028 (+~45%), with custom silicon targeted to more than double in FY2028 and exceed $10B by FY2029, and operating margin heading toward 38–40% on real operating leverage; it is prepaying ~$1B to secure scarce capacity. Two analytical cautions: (1) GAAP earnings are noisy and can sit far below OR above non-GAAP (acquisition accounting pushed Q1 FY2027 GAAP EPS to just $0.04 vs $0.80 non-GAAP; a tax benefit pushed FY2026 GAAP ABOVE non-GAAP) — judge the core on non-GAAP and cash flow; and (2) valuation is demanding — ~28x trailing / ~21x forward sales, with the ~$280 price trading ABOVE the ~$233 analyst consensus, so much future success is already in the price (52-week range $61→$324). The facts (record revenue, raised multi-year outlook, custom backlog, NVIDIA tie-up, margin leverage) are strong and well-documented; what is PRICED is durable ~40–45% growth, share held against Broadcom, and the custom/scale-up ramps landing on time. The core debate is execution + competition + valuation, not whether AI demand exists.
what_is_fact: Q1 FY2027 revenue record $2.418B (+28% YoY, +9% QoQ); non-GAAP gross margin 58.9%, non-GAAP operating margin 35%; non-GAAP net income $718M (EPS $0.80); GAAP EPS $0.04 (depressed by M&A accounting); record operating cash flow $639M. [2026-05-27]
Data center 76% of revenue ($1.8B, +27% YoY); communications & other $585M. [2026-05-27]
Raised outlook: FY2027 ~$11.5B (+~40%), FY2028 ~$16.5B (+~45%); custom >2x in FY2028 and >$10B target by FY2029; interconnect >70% YoY FY2027. [2026-05-27]
Expanded NVIDIA partnership (NVLink Fusion, optics, AI RAN) + NVIDIA equity stake; closed Celestial AI, XConn, Polariton; ~$1B FY2027 supplier prepayments. [2026-05-27]

ASSUMPTION: Marvell holds DSP/interconnect leadership and the custom ramp (incl. the new tier-1 XPU) executes toward >$10B by FY2029.
OPINION: Judge profitability on non-GAAP + cash flow — GAAP is distorted by M&A accounting and tax items.
OPINION: At ~28x sales and trading above the ~$233 consensus, the stock prices in years of success; downside is large if capex slows or Broadcom takes share.
what_to_watch_next: Q2 FY2027 results (~Aug 2026): did revenue hit the ~$2.7B guide and did GAAP normalize as promised?
Custom-silicon ramp — the new tier-1 XPU program and the 10+ attach programs vs the >2x FY2028 / >$10B FY2029 targets.
Interconnect growth rate (>70% FY2027) and DCI toward $1B annualized; scale-up optics (~$300M) and scale-up switching starting.
Hyperscaler cloud-capex commentary (the key swing factor) and any Broadcom share shifts.
Margin path toward the 38–40% operating model; ~$1B prepayments and capacity; share count/dilution.
